s01.text: You probably do this twenty times a day: double-clicking your home screen and furiously swiping every app away to save battery.

s02.text: Stop doing it right now. Swiping your apps closed does not save your battery — it actually drains it faster.

s03.text: Most users believe background apps are running live, burning your CPU and sucking power in the background.

s04.text: They are not. Modern operating systems freeze background apps in RAM, where they consume zero CPU cycles and practically zero wattage.

s05.text: When you force-quit an app, you purge its memory. Reopening it forces the processor to reload all code from flash storage, causing a massive power spike.

s06.text: Apple's head of software Craig Federighi was asked if quitting apps saves battery. His verified answer was just four words: 'No and No.'

s07.text: Your phone is engineered to manage its own memory. Leave the apps in RAM — and let your battery breathe.
